svg.text: GitOps conventions — the shape every app must land in
Argo CD with a Kustomize base/overlay layout. Applies to every app regardless of where the workload was migrated from.
.kiro/steering/gitops-conventions.md · inclusion: always — the largest single piece of the contract
Layout, naming, labels, image pinning, mandatory hardening, and the review rules that make one app's tree look like every other app's tree.
Where the project profile answers what are the values, this file answers what is the shape — and it is the file a reviewer is implicitly checking against.
Layout — base holds what is identical, overlays hold only what differs
If a value is the same in dev and prod, it belongs here — not duplicated twice.
Image digests, replica counts, secret paths, ingress hostnames. Keep them small.
If an overlay grows, the value probably belongs in base instead.
There is no dev-only app here. A prod overlay created at
promotion time is an overlay whose first ever build happens
The only seven things that may legitimately differ between overlays
anything else in one overlay and not the other is usually drift
Why it is allowed to differ
Prod trails dev by however long verification takes
Sized from observed usage per environment
Separate secrets per environment — one secretproviderclass.yaml per overlay
Each account has its own cert — alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/certificate-arn
Each account has its own WAF — alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/wafv2-acl-arn
A setting that is only exercised in prod is a setting that is only tested in prod. Keep the two overlays as close to identical as the environments allow.
Any Ingress annotation carrying an AWS account ID lives in the overlay, never in base
dev and prod are separate accounts, so these always differ
Nothing here contains an account ID, a hostname, or an ARN.
Everything account-bound is patched in, per cluster.
Gatekeeper validates ARN shape and image refs at gator test time — a bare token causes a false failure
Never write bare tokens like REPLACE_WITH_CERT_ID or REPLACE_WITH_ACTUAL_DIGEST into manifests.
Trailing digit differs per overlay (...0001 dev / ...0002 prod) so the two stay visually distinct. The WAFv2 webacl segment is the app name.
These exist only to pass kustomize build and gator test --deny-only in Git. They are not deployable.
Replace every dummy with a real ARN or digest before the app reaches a live cluster.
plain-manifest apps only — Helm-chart apps skip the second layer
sync wave: Namespace created & labelled first
Why two layers: the Namespace is created and labelled by a separate sync wave before any workload lands in it — which matters because admission policies gate on Namespace labels.
Never commit a feature branch name
Exception: do not set targetRevision to a branch for Helm chart repo sources (those with a chart: field) — they are versioned by chart version, not Git ref.
Naming — every manifest file is its Kubernetes kind, lowercased
never invent unrelated names: creds.yaml, netpol.yaml, app.yaml
Collision? Disambiguate with a suffix: deployment-<role>.yaml, configmap-passwd.yaml.
Several objects of one kind may share a file when they belong together (all NetworkPolicies in one).
Overlay patches follow the same rule with a -patch suffix:
Labels — the selector key is load-bearing
Workloads, ServiceAccount, NetworkPolicy, ConfigMap, Secret, etc.
Add part-of via the manifests kustomization.yaml:
app.kubernetes.io/name is the selector key. If it drifts
between the Deployment and the NetworkPolicy, the allow
policies match nothing and traffic is silently denied.
Images and promotion — base floats, overlays pin
manifests never point at the upstream registry
Every workload image is the existing ECR repo named after the app, in the dev account. Upstream sources (Docker Hub, GHCR, Quay, local build) are mirrored there first.
Keep the pin in exactly one file per overlay so a bump is a one-line diff. Pin even when no policy requires it: a tag can be re-pointed at different bytes, a digest cannot.
Promotion is copying the digest from overlays/dev-eks-1 to overlays/prod-eks-1. Prod runs the exact bytes verified in dev, and the diff shows precisely what is changing.
Three things are mandatory, not advisory
Explicit CPU and memory requests and limits on
every container — including init and sidecars.
Requests drive scheduling; limits cap blast radius.
Size from observed usage; else start small and raise
deny Ingress and Egress for every pod in the ns
DNS · HTTPS · Pod Identity · SSH · app ports
Do not combine allows into one policy.
Do not leave an app without the deny.
do not point both at a deep dependency check.
Slow start? Use startupProbe, not a long initialDelay.
Rollout safety and node drains are two different problems
confusing them is the single most common scar in this repo
Surge-first rolling updates keep a replicas: 1 service up during
an image or config rollout. Prefer this for web-facing Deployments.
Safe at replicas: 1 — a new pod comes up before the old one goes down.
Does NOT replace a PDB for node drains.
Cordon / drain, EKS Auto Mode and Karpenter node replacement.
Add only when the Deployment (or KEDA/HPA floor) runs at least 2 replicas.
No — remove the PDB or raise replicas
With replicas: 1, a minAvailable: 1 PDB blocks every voluntary eviction → DisruptionBlocked and stuck node replacement.
IAM lives in apps/<app>/iam.tf, applied separately from the manifests
Argo CD syncs. Two systems means ordering is your responsibility.
Adding a permission → apply Terraform first, then merge the manifest.
Removing one → merge manifest first, confirm unused, then apply Terraform.
A pod whose Pod Identity association does not exist yet starts normally and fails its
first AWS call — surfacing as an app error, not missing infrastructure.
Vendor a chart only when the fetch fails
Managed Argo CD often has one Git credential (e.g. CodeConnections) that
gets sent to non-Git HTTP endpoints and rejected, so chart fetches fail.
helm pull --untar -d apps/<app>/base/vendored/chart/, record upstream URL +
pinned version in a README, point the Application at the in-repo path.
Vendoring is a workaround, not a default.
Replicas owned by KEDA or an HPA
Set the manifest to the autoscaler floor (0 for KEDA, 1 for HPA) and add
ignoreDifferences on /spec/replicas — else Argo fights the autoscaler.
Every app must have a README — create it with the scaffold, do not defer it
1. Title #<app> and a short purpose paragraph. 2. ## Inputs and outputs — a required Mermaid flowchart LR with an inputs subgraph (queues, HTTP clients,
schedules, secrets, upstream APIs), the app or named workers in the middle, and an outputs subgraph (sinks, responses, downstream APIs, storage).
Labeled edges that say how each link works — protocol, env var, Pod Identity, CSI → env — not bare arrows. 3. Compact tables under the diagram. 4. Image / ECR, IAM, networking sections as needed.
Do not substitute a shallow "Client → ALB → Pod" architecture diagram.
Must pass repo lint: npx --yes markdownlint-cli2 "apps/<app>/README.md"
Use ASCII -> rather than Unicode arrows in docs and comments.
Markdown tables: compact pipe style with a space either side of every |.
one layout → one naming rule → one label key → base floats, overlays pin → mandatory hardening → a README that explains the data flow
